answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may place orders or earn reputation. If a sybil account is caught double-spending or coordinating fraud, its stake is forfeited, while identities that behave honestly can recover it. Splitting one attacker’s budget across an orchard of fake agents does not multiply that budget: each account needs its own lock, and detection burns real capital. The oasis of cheap pseudonyms becomes costly to maintain, and an atlas of identities offers no free way around the rule.
